summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and PEG dependence was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for fever and vomiting. Workup revealed a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus urinary tract infection and possible aspiration-related pneumonia. He was treated with linezolid for the VRE UTI and cefepime for the lung infection, with clinical improvement. A CT scan showed bladder wall thickening and diverticula, raising concern for chronic urinary retention; a Foley catheter was placed as he did not tolerate intermittent catheterization, and outpatient urodynamic testing was scheduled. A pressure- and moisture-related rash on the back was treated with topical steroids and antifungal powder. He completed a 7-day antibiotic course, remained stable, and was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, maintain the Foley catheter until urology follow-up, and resume all chronic medications including antiretrovirals and seizure prophylaxis.
